name: Heat maps

slide.title: Sprints 4 to 6 carry the heaviest commitments

body.p: Every team commits above 24 points while go-live prep peaks.
Commits above its 36-point capacity in sprints 4 to 6.
Load eases to 26 points or fewer everywhere before the freeze.

Highest access need and the lowest build effort in the map.
Already working; revisit after the revenue cycle program.

slide.title: Skills and sustainment are the widest readiness gaps

body.label: Widest gaps
body.title: Physicians and nurses
body.body: Both groups score 3 on buy-in or skills, the two levers that decide adoption.

body.label: Sustainment
body.title: No group is secure
body.body: Six of seven groups carry a gap of 2 or more once the team steps back.

body.label: Strength
body.title: Leaders and IT
body.body: Executives and the service desk are ready to coach others.

templates.name: Readiness heat map, site split

slide.title: Harbor Clinics are the least ready site

items.text: The only site with a critical gap, on tools, and a large gap on buy-in.
Urgent care staff cannot spare time for training.
No gap above small; use its super users to coach the others.

templates.name: Compact heat map, takeaway left

slide.title: Recovery is the weakest control

body.text: Four of five clinical systems have never tested a recovery.
Backups exist; the untested failover is the exposure.

items: Test failover for the imaging archive and the EHR before go-live.
Document recovery steps for the imaging archive, which scores worst on every control.
